reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly demonstrates that the exact hybrid-rolling process on the same alloy produces the claimed heterogeneous structure and achieves ~2000 MPa strength with ~8% ductility, supporting all key premises. E1 provides additional support for microcrack-arresting mechanisms in a related heterogeneous lamellar structure, though the specific back-stress hardening mechanism is not explicitly detailed in the cited passages.
premises: Cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling at ~600 °C refines the coarse lamellar colony into a nano-dual-phase heterogeneous structure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The resulting heterogeneous structure consists of ultrafine recrystallized regions, retained lamellae, and abundant phase boundaries.
This structure promotes strong back-stress hardening during tensile loading.
The structure activates microcrack-arresting mechanisms that improve ductility.
The combination of these mechanisms simultaneously increases room-temperature strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
